title: Finish painting a panel a coworker started, without repainting their work
instruction: Your coworker started painting this panel. Finish it with the paint roller: cover every bare spot, including any they missed, without repainting their work beyond a small overlap, and keep paint off the table.
context: Painters (O*NET 47-2141.00) often take over a surface someone else started, after a break or a shift change. Nothing marks what is left: it has to be read off the surface. A missed spot, called a holiday in coating inspection, gets the coat rejected and touched up; rolling over paint that has already dried wastes paint and time and leaves lap marks. Unlike wiping or cleaning, where covering more never hurts, this score is two-sided: every bare cell must be painted, including three small patches the coworker missed inside their own paint, but repainting their work beyond a 2 cm overlap costs score, and painting the whole panel scores 0. The robot must find where primer meets paint in the camera images, plan overlapping strokes that leave no gaps, touch up the missed patches precisely, stop at the boundary, and keep the roller's cover level on the panel.
setup: Dream Labs' YAM station (scene=station), both arms starting at their ready pose. World frame: origin between the arm bases, x forward, y to the left, z up; the table top is at z = 0.7475 m. Panel: primed MDF, 30 cm (x) by 40 cm (y) by 1.2 cm, fixed on the table, centred at x 0.235 m, y -0.02 m, built from flush rigid slabs. Bare off-white primer (sRGB 0.93, 0.92, 0.89): a 22 cm (x) by 21 cm (y) rectangle at x 0.125 to 0.345 m, y -0.18 to 0.03 m, and three 6 cm (x) by 3 cm (y) missed patches centred at (x 0.165, y 0.085), (x 0.255, y 0.135) and (x 0.305, y 0.075) m. Everything else is the coworker's dry blue paint (sRGB 0.16, 0.36, 0.78): a 4 cm border all round and the left 15 cm of the panel (that side's border included). For a real trial, mask the bare areas, paint the rest and let it dry. Paint roller, a 4-inch mini trim roller: a blue foam cover loaded with paint (4 cm across, 10 cm long, 20 g) spinning freely on a steel axle along x; a 5 mm zinc-plated wire frame from both axle ends, rising 2.5 cm to a cross bar 4 cm toward -y; and a straight yellow plastic handle, 2.4 x 2.4 x 11 cm, running on toward -y (frame and handle 70 g). It lies on a grey plastic drip tray (14 x 20 x 1 cm, fixed, centred at x 0.20 m, y -0.33 m), the cover centred at x 0.20 m, y -0.255 m, the handle's end on a fixed grey plastic block (4 x 2.5 x 3.3 cm) standing on the tray, so the handle is level. All objects share one rubber-like friction (static 1.2, dynamic 1.0), except the roller's wire frame and axle, which use the simulator's default (0.5 static and dynamic). The layout is fixed (-E object_jitter=0).
scoring: The panel is scored on a grid of 1 cm cells (30 x 40); in a real trial, count cells on a top photo through a 1 cm grid. A cell gets paint when it lies under the roller cover's lowest line (its centre within 5 mm of that line, along the cover's 10 cm), the axle is within 10 degrees of level, and the line over the cell is between 3 mm below and 1.5 mm above the panel top, so a cover with one end lifted paints only where it touches; cells between two touching control steps whose cover centres are up to 4 cm apart also get paint. Base score from the 516 bare cells (462 in the rectangle, 18 in each missed patch): 1.0 when all are painted; 0.8 at 98% or more (at most 10 missed); 0.6 at 95% or more; 0.4 at 80% or more; 0.2 at 50% or more; otherwise 0. Wasted cells are the coworker's cells whose centres are more than 2 cm from any bare area that the robot painted (in a real trial, read off the overhead video, since new paint matches theirs): up to 20 keeps the base score, 21 to 60 multiplies it by 0.75, 61 to 120 by 0.5, and more than 120 scores 0 (painting the whole panel wastes 367). Painting up to 2 cm into the coworker's paint is free. If any part of the roller comes within 1.5 mm of the table top while it is over the table and the cover is not painting the panel (paint on the table), the score is capped at 0.5. Score = base x multiplier, then the cap, at the end of the trial; a full score counts once it has held for 1 s (until then it reads 0.8), and holding it for 1 s ends the trial as a success.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed in simulation: every trial starts with only the coworker's paint. A real trial uses one pre-painted panel per trial (mask, paint and dry the coworker's areas beforehand) and a roller freshly loaded with paint, laid on the tray.
fidelity: The roller is built from primitives: a rigid foam cylinder on a frictionless axle joint (it rolls but doesn't compress) in a box handle and wire frame; a real trim roller's handle is angled, this one is straight. Paint is not a fluid: a 1 cm grid of painted cells, updated from the cover's pose each control step and drawn as thin blue tiles the cameras see. Contact is geometric. No drips, film or paint load; paint on the table is scored, not drawn. Friction 1.2/1.0 (wire frame 0.5).
